item.title: Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk - v3.2.39 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Fixes

  • ISE posture reports are ingested again — the Cisco ISE Analytics Reports input again copies the Posture reports (cisco:ise:analytics:registry, cisco:ise:analytics:hardware, and cisco:ise:analytics:applications) from ISE local disk into the SFTP repository before ingestion. A prior change skipped that copy for posture reports on the incorrect assumption that they were written directly to the repository, which left them stranded on disk so those sourcetypes produced no events. All report types are now transferred consistently.
  • Cyber Vision generic API input configuration no longer flagged invalid — the cisco_catalyst_cybervision_api input's logging_level setting is now declared in the input specification, so Splunk no longer logs an "Invalid key in stanza [cisco_catalyst_cybervision_api] … logging_level" error when validating inputs.conf.

Enhancements

  • ISE Analytics Reports pipeline health in the Data Collection Health dashboard — the ISE tab gains an Analytics Reports Pipeline section that tracks collection end to end: reports generated on ISE, transferred to the repository, ingested, and (for FullReports) cleaned off the ISE local disk. It shows a per-input pipeline funnel, pipeline runs over time, and a FullReports Left on ISE Disk indicator. Because ISE does not remove previous FullReport runs on its own, a FullReport left behind after a failed transfer accumulates on the ISE disk; this indicator is an early warning for disk fill-up. The signal is derived entirely from the add-on's own internal logs, so it works when the add-on runs on-premises and the dashboard is viewed in Splunk Cloud. The ISE Analytics Reports input now emits structured pipeline and report-cleanup telemetry to support these panels.

Upgrade notes

  • No reconfiguration required; upgrades are seamless.
  • Posture report events resume on the next collection run of the ISE Analytics Reports input; no change to inputs or repository settings is needed.
  • The new ISE Analytics Reports pipeline panels populate when that input's logging level is set to INFO; the FullReports-left-on-disk warning is emitted at WARNING and appears regardless. Panels and telemetry appear on the next collection run.

Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk collects and normalizes API telemetry from Cisco Catalyst Center, SD-WAN (vManage), ISE, and Cyber Vision through modular inputs. It includes CIM-aligned knowledge objects, backward-compatible DNAC/Catalyst sourcetype coverage, and built-in health monitoring for input status, errors, and API load.

item.title: Cisco Enterprise Networking for Splunk Platform - v3.2.10 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Dashboards & Usability

  • SD-WAN Change Audit dashboard refreshed: Added clearer setup guidance, collapsible prerequisites, better panel descriptions, summary metrics, and a focused change explorer for reviewing vManage administrative changes from cisco:sdwan:audit:logs.
  • SD-WAN before/after configuration review improved: The dashboard now uses the collector-provided audit_config_before and audit_config_after fields directly, so config comparison panels no longer rely on fragile position-based audit detail reconstruction.
  • SD-WAN audit setup guidance added: The dashboard now explains that customers need Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk version 3.2.38 or later, an SD-WAN Audit Logs input, and both Audit Log Details and Config Difference enabled to populate the detail and config-diff views.
  • Overview setup guidance added: The Overview dashboard now links to the required Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk and provides a concise setup checklist for production deployments: scope index macros first, enable data model acceleration second, then set summariesonly to true after acceleration reaches 100.00% Completed.
  • Index macro setup improved: cisco_catalyst_app_index and cisco_catalyst_sdwan_index now default to all indexes so first-run dashboards can find data before local macro configuration. The Overview dashboard includes helper searches that return paste-ready macro values for production scoping.
  • Step Reports access cleanup: Removed stale metadata that referenced an undefined cisco_catalyst_step_reports role, so Step Reports inherit the normal app view permissions.
  • App metadata cleanup: Declared light and dark theme support and removed stale install/runtime metadata from the packaged app configuration.
  • Cyber Vision vulnerability overview corrected: Updated the vulnerability dashboard so it uses the correct app index macro and aligns with the dedicated cisco:cybervision:vulnerabilities sourcetype.

Data Models & Fields

  • Expanded Cisco Catalyst data model coverage: Added child datasets for Catalyst Center interface health (cisco:dnac:devicehealth:interface), Cyber Vision vulnerabilities (cisco:cybervision:vulnerabilities), Cyber Vision components (cisco:cybervision:components), Cyber Vision flows (cisco:cybervision:flows), and SD-WAN SSE tunnel health (cisco:sdwan:ssetunnelhealth).
  • Data model acceleration defaults clarified: The packaged Cisco Catalyst data model now defines a 7-day acceleration summary range and staggered 5-minute schedule for admins who enable acceleration. The Hunk-only DFS block-size setting was removed.
  • SD-WAN audit data model fields added: Added the new SD-WAN audit detail and before/after config fields produced by Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk 3.2.38 to the SD-WAN audit child dataset, including audit_log_details, audit_config_before, audit_config_after, and related summary fields.
  • SD-WAN audit user field corrected: Added the correctly spelled audit_log_user field and updated app content to use it while preserving the previous audti_log_user field for backward compatibility.
  • Cross-app data model searches fixed: Exported the Cisco Catalyst data model together with its required base-search macros, cisco_catalyst_app_index and cisco_catalyst_app_sourcetypes, so external apps can run tstats searches against Cisco_Catalyst_App without data model root-object cache errors.
  • Packaged metadata export handling fixed: Updated the packaging scrub step to keep app-wide metadata private while preserving explicit per-object exports required by shared knowledge objects.

Upgrade notes

  • Upgrade the Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk from Splunkbase to version 3.2.38 or later to populate the newest sourcetypes and SD-WAN audit config-diff fields used by this app.
  • For the SD-WAN Change Audit dashboard, create an Audit Logs input in the Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk and enable both Audit Log Details and Config Difference. Without that input, no cisco:sdwan:audit:logs data is collected; without those checkboxes, the detail and before/after config panels remain empty.
  • Before enabling data model acceleration, use the Overview dashboard helper searches to populate cisco_catalyst_app_index and cisco_catalyst_sdwan_index. The defaults search all indexes to avoid empty first-run dashboards, but scoped macros are strongly recommended for production performance and data boundaries.
  • If data model acceleration is enabled, use at least a 7-day summary range, or increase to 30 days or more if users search longer windows and the environment can support it. When acceleration status reaches 100.00% Completed, set the summariesonly macro to summariesonly=true for best dashboard performance.

item.title: Supply Chain and AI Threat Intelligence Platform - v1.1.11 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

This is the first update since the initial release (v1.0.0). It includes the following changes.

Compatibility

  • Splunk Enterprise 9.2+ and Splunk Cloud
  • Standalone and distributed deployments (indexer cluster + search head cluster)
  • Splunk Enterprise Security is not required — ES integration is an optional enhancement (Professional tier includes native Risk-Based Alerting integration when ES is present)
  • The Federal Plus POA\&M Generator custom search command targets on-prem and air-gapped Splunk Enterprise only; all other features, including everything below, run on Splunk Cloud

New Capabilities

  • Critical & High-Risk Exposure (all tiers) — home dashboard now shows a real-time count of critical and high-severity vulnerabilities in your ingested SBOMs, calculated from your actual component data. Adjacent to it, an actively-exploited-vulnerability awareness indicator references CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog — on Community tier this flags that active exploitation may be present without a specific count; on Professional and above, the full KEV-matched count and remediation tracking are available.
  • Compliance Gap Visibility (all tiers) — home dashboard now shows your real, personalized compliance gap percentage for your configured primary framework (e.g., "38% of your in-scope PCI DSS 4.0 controls have gaps") — a genuine calculation from your own data, not a placeholder. Control-by-control evidence, remediation tracking, and exportable reports remain Professional and above.
  • Long-Unpatched Critical Exposure (all tiers) — new home dashboard panel identifies critical/high-severity vulnerabilities unpatched 180+ days, surfacing negligence/audit-finding risk distinct from active-exploitation alerts. Available at every tier including free Community; remediation tracking to act on findings is Professional and above.
  • Compound Risk Correlation (Enterprise, Federal Plus) — new dedicated dashboard view identifies applications with both an active MITRE ATLAS AI-threat detection and one or more critical or actively-exploited vulnerable components, correlating two previously-separate risk signals into one view. Requires a one-time setup step: map your AI/LLM application hosts to their SBOM products in Setup Section 1d (AI Application Mapping).
  • AI/ML Bill of Materials (Professional and above; risk classification on Enterprise and Federal Plus) — catalogs AI/ML model components from your SBOMs (architecture, training data sources, full lineage/pedigree) on Professional tier and above. Additionally flags models using known-insecure serialization formats versus safer alternatives, correlated into the same risk-scoring context as your CVE/KEV findings — available on Enterprise and Federal Plus.

Licensing

  • License enforcement rebuilt on Ed25519 asymmetric digital signatures (RFC 8032). The app now ships only a public verification key — no secret of any kind is present in the package, and license keys can be created only by GIC Engineering Consultants. Validation remains fully offline and air-gap compatible: no phone-home, no key-server lookup.
  • Breaking change: license keys issued for versions prior to 1.1.0 use a retired format and will not validate. Contact contact@gicengineeringconsultants.com for replacement keys.

Correctness Fixes

  • Version comparison now handles prerelease and qualifier identifiers with numeric-aware ordering, correctly ranks Java/Maven release qualifiers, and ignores build metadata.
  • OSV vulnerability correlation is now version-aware at every correlation site: CVE matches are checked against the fixed version, so patched components no longer report already-remediated CVEs as still open.
  • NVD version-range correlation fix: each CVE now stays correctly paired with its own version bounds (previously a silent cap could desync CVEs from their ranges on high-CVE components), and results now correctly reach POA\&M population.
  • Severity classification corrected: CVSS vector strings and score data are now parsed into proper severity levels instead of collapsing to "unknown"; the bundled vulnerability data was regenerated accordingly.
  • Multi-license component handling fixed end-to-end: every SBOM ingestion path now produces one consistent, canonical representation of multi-license components. License Risk classification now correctly evaluates each license in a multi-license component individually, so a component isn't missed just because its risky license is bundled with a safe one. Affects License Risk and Compliance reporting.

Security Hardening

  • Hardened role-based access controls — search access for each role (Viewer, Analyst, Admin) is now scoped more precisely to only the data indexes each role actually requires.
  • Browser-based license activation transport hardened so keys are no longer at risk of corruption in transit through the Splunk Web proxy.
  • Path-traversal protection added to CSV export.
  • SBOM XML parsing hardened against entity-expansion (XML bomb) denial-of-service payloads. Valid SBOMs are unaffected.
  • File-read paths for SBOM ingestion are now strictly contained to the app's own spool directory.
  • Privileged configuration commands are now access-gated to admin-tier roles, closing a path where they were reachable more broadly than intended.
  • License keys, API keys, and tokens no longer pass through search strings, removing them from audit/job-history visibility. All credential entry now goes through the Setup page's single gated path.
  • Duplicate vulnerability-correlation events eliminated — CVE matches are now indexed exactly once per unique match instead of being re-collected on every run.

Platform & Documentation

  • Corrected the home dashboard's vulnerability drill-down navigation so it lands on the pre-filtered, relevant detail view rather than a generic unfiltered list.
  • Corrected a configuration comment describing MITRE ATLAS detection rule scheduling — documentation-only, no change to detection behavior; AI-threat detection has been running as expected all along.
  • Removed version number display from in-app surfaces (About page, dashboard footers) in favor of the Splunkbase listing as the single, always-current source for version and release history.


Short Description:
Unifies software supply chain risk (SBOM/SCA), MITRE ATLAS AI-threat detection, and nine-framework compliance in one Splunk app — with FedRAMP-ready audit exports and no external security product required.


Description:
SCIP unifies software composition analysis (SCA), supply chain risk monitoring, and AI threat detection in one Splunk app. Ingest SBOMs, correlate components against live vulnerability intelligence (OSV, NVD, CISA KEV, EPSS), detect adversarial AI/ML threats with MITRE ATLAS, and assess compliance posture across nine global frameworks — with detection logic written as transparent SPL you can open and read, and no external security product required. CAPABILITIES - SBOM ingestion — file-drop or HEC, supporting CycloneDX (JSON/XML) and SPDX (JSON) - Vulnerability correlation — daily OSV feed (264,944+ records across 5 ecosystems) with PURL-based correlation; NVD CPE-based correlation; CISA KEV matching with BOD 22-01 SLA tracking; EPSS exploit-probability scoring - Supply Chain Risk Score — 0–100 global and per-application risk scoring weighted by severity, KEV status, and EPSS - Vendor Risk — per-vendor risk aggregation and letter-grading across your SBOM portfolio - SBOM Drift Detection — baseline-vs-current component change tracking - License Compliance — GPL/AGPL/copyleft detection and license-risk classification - MITRE ATLAS Detection — 66 detection rules for adversarial AI/ML threats - Compliance Gap Assessment — nine frameworks: PCI DSS 4.0, NIST CSF 2.0, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA Security Rule, EU Cyber Resilience Act, FedRAMP / RMF / CISA, DORA, FDA 524B Premarket Cybersecurity, SEBI CSCRF - POA&M & FedRAMP Workflow — POA&M dashboard, monthly ConMon package builder, BOD 22-01 SLA tracking, deviation request workflow. Dashboards always available; automated POA&M generation is opt-in from Setup - Audit-ready exports — FedRAMP POA&M Workbook (R3.0 and R2.1), SSP Appendix M Integrated Inventory, Deviation Request Form (Template 2.1 / Aug 2024) - Component Search — instant cross-SBOM component lookup (available in the free Community tier) - Compound Risk — correlates active MITRE ATLAS AI-threat detections with vulnerable components on the same application, surfacing compounding risk neither signal shows alone (Enterprise and Federal Plus) - AI/ML Bill of Materials — catalogs AI/ML model components from your SBOMs (architecture, training data, lineage) with insecure-serialization-format risk flagging (Professional and above; risk classification detail on Enterprise and Federal Plus) TIERS Community (free), Professional, Federal, Enterprise, Federal Plus. Feature availability gated by license tier; contact us for tier comparison. SUPPORT GIC Engineering Consultants — contact@gicengineeringconsultants.com

item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Ensign ElasticSearch Data Integrator — v2.0.1

Compatibility: Splunk Enterprise 9.4 (Python 3.9) and Splunk 10 (Python 3.13); Elasticsearch 8.x and 9.x. Upgrading in place preserves your Elasticsearch cluster profiles, data inputs and checkpoints.

Version 2.0 is a major-architecture release. The add-on has been fully rebuilt on the modern Splunk add-on (UCC) framework, and the checkpoint engine now supports reliable KVStore storage with lossless backend migration.

v2.0.1 — KVStore checkpoint fix & migration

  • Fix: KVStore checkpoint storage. The first checkpoint write to KVStore previously failed silently, so the collection appeared empty. Writes now insert correctly, and any KVStore read/write failure is logged instead of being swallowed.
  • New: Checkpoint backend migration. Switching Configuration > Checkpoint between File and KVStore now moves the existing checkpoint state (timestamp bookmark, deduplication guard and scroll state) to the newly selected backend and clears the old one. The copy is verified before the source is deleted, so no checkpoint data is lost if the target backend is unavailable.
  • New: The KVStore checkpoint collections are now viewable for inspection: | inputlookup es_checkpoint_store and | inputlookup es_seen_ids_store.

v2.0.0 — Rebuilt on the modern Splunk add-on framework

  • The add-on has been fully rebuilt on the current Splunk Universal Configuration Console (UCC) framework. The legacy Add-on Builder runtime has been removed entirely: the modular input now runs on the standard Splunk modular-input SDK and solnlib, and the configuration REST handlers use splunktaucclib.
  • 100% pure-Python and platform-independent — no compiled or OS-specific binaries are bundled.
  • The configuration UI has been regenerated on the current UCC (React) framework.
  • Functionally equivalent to the 1.5.x line: automatic Elasticsearch 8.x / 9.x client selection, KVStore checkpoints with smart bidirectional fallback, a single-term DSL query filter, multi-node cluster topology and health monitoring, and the diagnostic search commands (escheck_connection, escheck_config, escheck_indexes).

Also fixed since the previously published release (1.5.2)

  • Corrected several runtime and UI messages that were displayed in a non-English language; all user-facing text is now English (for example, the "Elasticsearch 9.x" version-selection message). No functional change.

Runtime notes

  • On Splunk 10 (Python 3.10+) the Elasticsearch 9.x native client is used; on Splunk 9.4 the Elasticsearch 8.19.3 client is used, which remains fully compatible with Elasticsearch 9.x servers via REST API compatibility mode.
  • Selecting Elasticsearch 9.x on a runtime that cannot support it (for example Splunk 9.4) is rejected on save with an actionable message; choose Auto-Detect or Elasticsearch 8.x instead.
  • After upgrading, hard-refresh the browser (Ctrl+F5) or use a private window so the regenerated configuration UI is not hidden by a cached copy.


Short Description:
Splunk modular input for ingesting data from Elasticsearch 8.x and 9.x clusters. Dual ES client (auto-selected by runtime), multi-cluster profiles, DSL query filters, scroll-based pagination with crash recovery, document-level deduplication, KVStore checkpoints, SSL/TLS, proxy, and custom SPL diagnostic commands. Full GUI configuration.


Description:
Ensign ElasticSearch Data Integrator is a Splunk modular input add-on for ingesting data from Elasticsearch 8.x and 9.x clusters into Splunk via the Elasticsearch REST API. Built on the Splunk UCC Framework (Add-on Builder), it provides a full GUI-driven configuration experience through Splunk Web — no manual file editing required. Key Features: • Multi-cluster Elasticsearch profile management via Splunk UI • Multi-node cluster support with comma-separated hosts and node sniffing/auto-discovery • Dual ES client library: automatically selects elasticsearch-py 9.4.1 (native) on Splunk 10 or elasticsearch-py 8.19.3 (REST API compatibility mode) on Splunk 9.4 • Per-cluster ES version override (Auto-Detect / 8.x / 9.x) with runtime capability gating • Time-based data fetching with configurable date field and ES Scroll API pagination • Single-term DSL query filter with input validation (fail-closed) • Crash-resilient scroll recovery with dedicated checkpoint directory • KVStore checkpoint storage with smart bidirectional fallback — enables SHC-native replication • Document-level deduplication guard (rolling 50,000 IDs per stanza) • SSL/TLS certificate verification enabled by default with custom CA support • Splunk CA auto-discovery for secure internal REST communication • Global proxy support with Splunk-native credential encryption • Custom sourcetype override per input stanza • Custom SPL diagnostic commands: escheck_connection, escheck_config, escheck_indexes • Comprehensive internal log parsing for taensignelasticsearchaddon:log • Preflight cluster health check before every collection run • 5W1H audit logging on all administrative operations • Minimum polling interval enforcement (15 seconds) • Adjustable log level (DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR) • No pre-compiled binaries — pure Python, runs on any platform Compatibility: • Elasticsearch: 8.x and 9.x (NOT compatible with 7.x or earlier) • Splunk Enterprise: 9.4+ (Python 3.9) and 10.x (Python 3.13) • Network: HTTPS access to target Elasticsearch cluster(s)

item.title: Whiteboard App - v0.3.71 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

# Release Notes

Highlights of recent Whiteboard App releases. For the full change list of any version, see the [GitHub Releases page](https://github.com/bautt/splunk-whiteboard-app/releases).

---

## v0.3.71 — 2026-07-10

**Splunk Cloud compatibility fix**

- Fixed a version mismatch that failed Splunk Cloud AppInspect (SLIM validation + semver): `app.manifest` had drifted to `0.3.65` while `app.conf` was newer, so the package could not be SSAI-installed on Classic Splunk Cloud.

- The build now treats `src/web/lib/version.js` as the single source of truth and syncs the version/build into `default/app.conf` and `app.manifest` automatically, so they can never drift again.

- Updated the app manifest description ("templates" → "example boards").

---

## v0.3.70 — 2026-07-10

**Board list layout & wording**

- Renamed **Starter boards** to **Example boards** throughout the app and docs.

- Your own boards now appear **first**; the shipped **Example boards** section moved to the **bottom** of the list.

- Fixed the cramped board card footer: **Open** is now a full-width button with the **Duplicate · Export · Copy link · Delete** actions on their own row below (no more truncated "Op…" button).

---

## v0.3.69 — 2026-07-10

**Starter boards replace the template concept**

- The board list now has a **Starter boards** section (Splunk Platform, Cisco Data Fabric, SVA C1/C11 & C3/C13). Click **Use** to create your own editable private copy and open it — the shipped originals never change, so app updates can't overwrite your work.

- **Duplicate** action on every board card makes a private copy (`\ (copy)`), so branching off any board (including a shared one) is one click.

- The separate **Templates** tab and the user-saved-template feature (with its 30-version history) have been removed. Reusing a layout across a team is now: make a board, share it, and colleagues **Duplicate** it.

- Existing user-saved templates are automatically **migrated to shared boards** on first load after upgrade.

**Uninstall cleanup**

- The **About** tab has a new *Danger zone* with **Delete all whiteboard data** — a guarded (type-to-confirm) action that purges every board, its history/snapshots, thumbnails, and legacy template data from KV Store before uninstalling the app.

---

## v0.3.68 — 2026-07-10

**SVA architecture templates**

- New prebuilt templates: **SVA C3/C13 — SHC Single Site** (Search Head Cluster) and **SVA C1/C11 — Single Site** (standalone search heads), with Splunk shape icons and doc links.

- Board generators (`scripts/generate-c3c13-shc-board.py`, `scripts/generate-c1c11-board.py`) and shared layout helpers for tight-fit text and baselines.

**Export all as ZIP**

- **Export all** now downloads a `.zip` archive with one `\.whiteboard.json` file per board (same format as single-board **Export**), instead of a single combined collection JSON.

- Legacy collection exports can still be imported via **Import board…**.

---

## v0.3.65 — 2026-07-10

**Board previews in the list**

- Each board card now shows a thumbnail preview of its content, so boards are easy to tell apart at a glance.

- Previews are stored in a dedicated `whiteboard_thumbnails` KV collection and refreshed shortly after edits are saved. Boards that don't yet have a stored preview generate one on demand the first time they scroll into view, then cache it for next time.

- Deleting a board also removes its stored preview.

---

## v0.3.64 — 2026-07-10

**Import & export from the board list**

- **Import board…** in the list toolbar loads one or more `.json` exports (single board or a legacy "export all" collection), creating them as private boards. Multiple files can be selected at once.

- **Export** on each board card downloads that board as `\.whiteboard.json`.

- **Export all** downloads every accessible board as individual `.whiteboard.json` files inside a ZIP archive.

---

## v0.3.63 — 2026-07-10

**Smarter entry page**

- First run (no saved boards) now opens straight onto an empty whiteboard instead of an empty list. Once any board exists, the app opens on the board list.

**About tab as a quick guide**

- The About tab now embeds a concise user guide with a **TL;DR** (build a whiteboard, use shapes & libraries, group & assign order, present) plus sections for getting started, drawing/shapes/libraries, grouping & presenting, and export/sharing — with links to the full README, release notes, and developer guide.

---

## v0.3.62 — 2026-07-10

**Theme reliability (readable in dark or light)**

- The app now reads Splunk Web's *actual* theme via Splunk's theme API (`getUserTheme`) instead of guessing from the OS `prefers-color-scheme`. Fixes unreadable text when the OS/browser is in dark mode but Splunk Web is light (or vice versa).

**Duplicate boards / delete-safety (data-loss fix)**

- Boards are de-duplicated by key, so a board no longer appears twice (once "Shared", once "Private"). This removes the trap where deleting one card deleted the single underlying record for both.

- Legacy boards (created before RBAC, with no visibility field) are classified as **shared**, and a board's scope is aligned to its visibility so edits/deletes target the correct namespace.

**Template appearance saved & restored**

- Saving a board as a template now stores its canvas theme and background; applying the template restores that appearance. Previously user templates lost theme/background on save and apply. Template revisions capture appearance too.

---

## v0.3.61 — 2026-07-10

**RBAC hardening & sharing safety**

- Granted `write` on the `whiteboard_revisions` KV collection — fixes silent autosave-history failures for non-privileged users on shared boards.

- `shareBoard` is now failure-safe/idempotent (key-preserving upsert, best-effort history migration, surfaced warnings).

- Optimistic `updated_at` conflict check on board writes and autosave, with a reload/overwrite banner; autosave pauses on conflict so concurrent edits are never clobbered.

**UI polish**

- Visibility toggle and filter tabs now use Splunk `RadioBar`/`TabBar` (theme-aware, accessible).

- Share and delete confirmations use Splunk `Modal` instead of native `confirm()`.

**Template fixes**

- Templates apply their intended theme/background on load (fixes Splunk Platform loading in light mode).

- Splunk Platform ships as **light** and **dark** variants; Cisco Data Fabric templates default to dark.

- Reordered Platform build steps so the Correlate/Analyze pillar reveals fully before Act/Automate.

**Navigation & libraries**

- Opening a board pushes a history entry, so the browser Back button returns to the board list instead of exiting to the About tab.

- Wired up Excalidraw `useHandleLibrary` + `libraryReturnUrl` so libraries install from libraries.excalidraw.com and persist across reloads.

---

## v0.3.59 — 2026-07-10

- `state_change_requires_restart \= true` in `app.conf` — Splunk Manager shows **Restart Required** after install/upgrade/enable/disable, avoiding HTTP 500 when opening the app before Splunk Web picks up HTML templates.

- README: Sharing & access section; post-install restart note.

---

## v0.3.58 — 2026-07-10

- Documentation: README redesigned as an Excalidraw-first user guide (templates, shapes/SVGs, export/import, Present mode); build/deploy/extension guides moved to `DEVELOPER.md`.

- Build / Present: reveal-on-click workflow improvements; new `scripts/assign-reveal-order.py` helper.

- Cisco Data Fabric template asset refreshed; board bundle import/export refinements.

---

## v0.3.54 — 2026-06-22

- SSAI / SLIM validation: removed invalid `python.version` from `app.conf`; set `platformRequirements.splunk.Enterprise` to `"*"`.

- Splunkbase listing copy and README screenshot updates.

---

## v0.3.53 — 2026-06-22

- Splunkbase readiness: package `README.md` and `PRIVACY.md` in the tarball; manifest updated with release date, company, privacy policy, and release-notes paths.

- Enabled `check_for_updates`; added `splunkbase.md` listing copy; documented minimum Splunk Enterprise/Cloud 9.0.0.

---

## v0.3.51 — 2026-06-18

- Fixed custom colour field showing brown after selecting the Splunk navy preset (removed incorrect hardcoded dark-mode value).

- Preserve `displayBackgroundColor` when Excalidraw `onChange` fires after appearance-panel updates.

---

## v0.3.50 — 2026-06-18

- Canvas dark mode: persist `displayBackgroundColor` so a picked colour survives light ↔ dark toggles (fixes Splunk navy `#001B3A` shifting).

- Performance: replaced slow brute-force colour inversion with a cached iterative solver.

- Added Splunk navy (`#001b3a`) swatch to the Canvas appearance panel.

---

## v0.3.48 — 2026-06-18

- Board delete cascades removal of revision and snapshot KV rows.

- Autosave persists correctly for cleared canvases after Excalidraw mounts.

- Templates: **Replace board** replaces misleading **Apply**, with an unsaved-changes warning.

- 5 MB size cap on imported Excalidraw library JSON; portable `perl` telemetry-check build step.

- New Federated Search architecture example board.

---

## v0.3.47 — 2026-06-18

- Synced `app.manifest` with `app.conf`; declared Splunk Cloud support.

- Cascade-delete board history on board delete; fixed autosave for cleared canvases.

- Library import size limit, portable build tooling, README updates.

---

## v0.3.36 — 2026-06-17

- **About tab** showing app version and README link.

- **Dark canvas**: theme toggle auto-applies charcoal/black or white background.

- **Template SVG icons** rehydrate on save/apply so placeholders no longer appear.

- **Revision history**: auto-revisions on save plus named snapshots in the History panel.

- Dedicated Canvas appearance sidebar tab for theme and background colour.

Key features: - Automatic field mapping with type coercion (integers, booleans) for clean data delivery - Batched HTTP transport with configurable batch size and timeout - API key stored securely in Splunk's encrypted credential storage (storage/passwords) - Credentials configured once via the setup page, used automatically by both the search command and alert action - Per-use credential overrides via inline arguments or alert action parameters - Splunk internal fields automatically stripped; _raw preserved for full event context - SSL verification enabled by default with optional override for development environments This app is designed for security teams using Intruex as their AI SOC platform and Splunk as their SIEM. It bridges the gap between detection in Splunk and automated analysis in Intruex. Requires an active Intruex account and API key.

item.title: Adjutant AI (AI Workbench) - v1.8.4 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Adjutant AI (formerly AI Workbench) — Release notes

What's new, improved, and fixed in each release, in plain language. This is the
customer-facing summary used for the Splunkbase release-notes section; the
full technical changelog lives in the project's detailed release notes.

Last updated: 2026-07-09

About version numbers. Releases once numbered 0.10–0.13 were renumbered to
1.0–1.3 to reflect production maturity — no behaviour changed. The current release is
1.8.4 — async playbook execution over MCP (start / status / results) plus the new
Outcome Ledger (an Enterprise executive/audit dashboard), built on 1.8.3
(a security‑hardening release: OWASP + dependency + anti‑ransomware audit), 1.8.2 (Splunk
Edge Processor data‑quality awareness and keyless Azure OpenAI authentication), 1.8.1
(support‑diagnosis fixes) and 1.8.0 (agent telemetry & OCSF export, content packs,
all‑tiers data‑quality checks, Splunk 10.x readiness, Dashboard Studio version‑awareness). The
1.7.0 ServiceNow integration and the 1.5.0 "Data Foundation & MCP OAuth" themes are
included below.

1.8.4 "Async playbooks over MCP"

Run Adjutant AI playbooks from an AI agent over the Model Context Protocol with a reliable
start → poll → fetch pattern. A playbook can take several minutes, but AI tool calls are
subject to short timeouts you don't control (the MCP server, the client, proxies), so trying to
wait for the answer in one call is fragile. Now every call returns in seconds.

New / Improved

  • Start returns immediately. adjutantai_start_playbook (the old adjutantai_run_playbook
    name is removed) hands back a run id at once with a hint on how to poll.
  • Check progress with adjutantai_get_playbook_status — queued, running, completed, or
    failed (a run that hit a recoverable error and is auto‑retrying is reported as still running,
    not failed), with guidance to stop polling after ~15 minutes.
  • Fetch the verdict with adjutantai_get_playbook_results once completed — condensed by
    default, or the full result on request; a partial result is clearly labelled.
  • Tenant‑safe. One team can't read another team's run; unknown or expired run ids simply
    return "not found." Run records are kept for 7 days by default.
  • Try it out of the box: start MCP Example: Read-only Health Check under Org/BU
    DFLT/DFLT (the read‑only reference playbook shipped on every install), then poll and fetch.

Requires the inbound MCP server and the Backend Ask Service to be enabled. No configuration
changes. Restart Splunk after upgrading.

Also in 1.8.4 — the Outcome Ledger (Enterprise)

A single screen that answers what a CEO, CISO or auditor actually asks: what did agentic AI do
for us this period, was it any good, what did it save, what did it cost — and can I see the
evidence for one run? It assembles data the app already records (unattended‑run history,
analyst agreement, run telemetry, LLM spend) into one executive/audit view. It adds no new
data collection and sends nothing to any external service.

New

  • The dashboard (Adjutant AI ▸ Outcome Ledger): headline tiles (investigations run
    without a human, how often analysts agreed with the AI — with the sample size and coverage
    shown, benign/false‑positive runs auto‑closed, analyst hours saved, LLM spend, typical time to
    a verdict), the mix of AI conclusions over time, agreement by case type, a weekly ledger, and
    an evidence table you can click through to the full detail of any single run. A footer
    spells out every assumption so a number is never quoted out of context.
  • Safe to hand to an auditor. What each viewer may see is decided on the server from their
    own identity — never from the page — and fails closed. In this release the dashboard is for
    Splunk administrators; scoped, delegated auditor access is the next step.
  • Is the AI real, or just performing? An Efficacy Trend panel puts run volume against how
    often analysts agreed, over time. If the agent runs more while analysts increasingly override
    it, the panel says so ("scaling faster than trust") instead of hiding it behind a healthy‑looking
    headline — and on too little feedback it honestly says the sample is too thin to judge.
  • Honest numbers. Effort saved is shown as time (with the per‑case assumption stated), spend
    is the real logged cost, and the per‑investigation efficiency signal is token usage — never an
    invented cost estimate.

Enterprise feature. No effect on any existing behaviour. Restart Splunk after upgrading.

1.8.3 "Security hardening"

A security‑focused release. Adjutant AI was put through an independent OWASP Top 10 (web and
LLM), dependency‑vulnerability, and "AI‑driven ransomware" review. The headline: no critical
issues, no default passwords or keys, no vulnerable components that ship to you, and the
assistant cannot be turned into an attack tool. Confirmed issues are fixed; a plain‑language,
reviewer‑ready write‑up ships in the app as SECURITY_AUDIT.md.

Improved / Fixed

  • Credentials stay server‑side. Provider API keys and keyless Azure sign‑in secrets are
    never sent to the browser or to other users in your tenant. (The free‑tier browser API‑key
    path is unchanged.)
  • Prompts stay in your audit index, not Splunk's internal logs.
  • Stronger multi‑tenant isolation for investigation results and knowledge sources.
  • You confirm every change. Closing a notable, setting a disposition, an
    ITSI/TrackMe/ServiceNow write, or overwriting a saved dashboard now asks for explicit
    confirmation first. Read‑only questions and new private dashboards are unaffected.
  • General hardening: cleaner errors, tighter sign‑in redirects, safer content‑pack imports,
    email TLS verification on by default.

No new features or config changes. Restart Splunk after upgrading.

1.8.2 "Edge Processor data-quality + keyless Azure OpenAI auth"

Keyless Azure OpenAI (Microsoft Entra ID / managed identity). Connect Azure OpenAI without a
static API key — using a Microsoft Entra ID service principal or a managed identity, governed by
your Entra tenant. Runs entirely server-side (no token reaches the browser), supports Public and
US Gov clouds, and adds a one-click Test connection that names exactly what to fix if something
is off. Connecting Azure with a plain API key still works on every tier; the keyless Entra path
is an Enterprise capability.

Edge Processor data-quality

If your data passes through Splunk Edge Processor before it reaches Splunk, some parsing,
timestamping, dropping and routing happens upstream — where Splunk's own internal logs and
feed-health tools can't see it. This release teaches the assistant to look at that hop.

  • New "Edge Processor → Splunk data-quality check". Ask the assistant to check an Edge
    Processor feed and it reads Edge Processor's own operational metrics (throughput, dropped
    events, failed destination sends, and queue backpressure) and tells you, in plain language,
    whether data is being silently lost or delayed before it lands — with a proof dashboard.
  • Honest by design. If Edge Processor telemetry isn't reaching your Splunk yet, the
    assistant says so and gives you the exact setup steps (on-premises vs Splunk Cloud) instead of
    inventing a clean bill of health. It reports at the pipeline level and is clear that per-event
    checks need a small addition to your Edge Processor pipeline.
  • Folds into the readiness verdict. Edge Processor joins Splunk parsing, feed-health, and
    Cribl as another "is this data actually good?" signal, and can cap the Data Quality Score when
    it finds upstream loss.
  • Read-only and available on every tier, exactly like the existing Cribl check.

1.8.1 "Cleaner support diagnosis"

A small maintenance update over 1.8.0 (front-end only).

  • More accurate "Report an issue" diagnosis. The automated issue classifier no longer
    mislabels a session that finished normally — one that completed and produced its dashboard — as
    having "run out of tool steps." The suspected-issue summary in your support bundle is now cleaner
    for healthy, tool-heavy sessions.

1.8.0 "Agent telemetry & OCSF export, content packs & all-tiers data quality"

New — your SOC can watch the agent (OCSF telemetry).

  • Adjutant AI emits its own activity as OCSF. Every LLM call, tool / MCP / ServiceNow call,
    configuration change, unattended run verdict, and policy refusal (the proof the controls
    actually fire) can be written as open-standard OCSF events to a Splunk index your Enterprise
    Security / SOC already watches — mapped to CIM via the community OCSF-CIM Add-On. Your SOC
    monitors our agent the same way it monitors everything else: on-prem, with no cloud egress.
  • You stay in control. It is off by default and Enterprise-gated. You provision and name
    the index     (the app ships no indexes.conf). Routing and content are resolved per Organisation
    / Business Unit    ; content export is denied by default and never exceeds your audit (DPIA) ceiling,
    with a server-side redaction check before anything is written.
  • See it immediately. A shipped admin dashboard — Adjutant AI — Behaviour (OCSF) — shows the
    token trend, model mix, tool/MCP egress with identity, the refusal and finding feeds, and a per-run
    drilldown, all on raw OCSF (no CIM Add-On required).

New — update Adjutant's content without waiting for a whole new app release.

  • Content packs. Almost everything Adjutant does well lives in its content — the
    skills, knowledge, and templates (playbooks). A content pack is a single, versioned
    file that lets us ship a corrected or improved content set straight to your install, and
    lets your admin apply it safely — no Splunkbase re-vetting cycle for a content fix.
  • Your changes are protected. Applying a pack upgrades only the items you haven't
    changed    . Anything your team has customised is left exactly as-is and clearly listed,
    never silently overwritten — and your Org/BU scoping is always preserved. After an
    import you get a per-item report, and the list of items that need manual reconciliation
    is downloadable as a CSV.
  • Safe by design. Every pack carries an integrity check, so a tampered or truncated
    file is refused. Imports live on the Backups page, which also shows which content
    version you're currently on — run a backup first and you can roll back in one click.
  • Retire without deleting. A pack can mark an item retired — it stays installed but
    is hidden and switched off everywhere (it can't be picked, run, or used by the
    assistant). An admin can re-enable it at any time by removing the tag.

Improved — data-quality checks for everyone, and Splunk 10.x readiness.

  • Data-quality ingestion checks are now available on every edition, including the free
    tier.     Checking whether a feed is actually landing and parsing correctly — on
    index=_internal, through TrackMe, and through Cribl Stream — is a baseline
    capability now, not a Professional add-on.
  • Ready for Splunk Enterprise 10.2 and 10.4. The app declares Python 3.9 and 3.13
    compatibility and has been audited against the 10.x platform changes (dashboards, the web
    framework, KV Store). Your admin still completes the standard KV Store engine migration as
    part of any 10.x upgrade.
  • Smarter Dashboard Studio building. The assistant now works from a single,
    version-aware map of what Dashboard Studio supports on your Splunk version — it won't
    reach for a chart type your version can't render, and when your Splunk is newer than what
    we've documented it builds conservatively and verifies the result.

Fixed.

  • Fewer false "the dashboard is blank" errors. A heavy Dashboard Studio dashboard that
    renders fine but slowly is no longer wrongly reported as blank — the assistant confirms the
    panels actually returned data before deciding, so it stops wasting a retry on a dashboard
    that was already correct. A genuinely blank dashboard is still caught.
  • TrackMe panels only when they belong. Fixed a rule that pushed a TrackMe feed-health
    panel onto every generated dashboard (and used a lookup that fails outside the TrackMe
    app). The assistant now adds a feed-health panel only when it's actually relevant, using a
    method that works in your app.

1.7.0 "ServiceNow integration" (included in the 1.8.0 release)

Renamed to Adjutant AI. The app is now Adjutant AI (formerly "AI Workbench").
This is a display-name change only — the in-app title (the easter egg now lives on
the dot of the "i" in Adjutant Ai), the app label, the documentation, and the
assistant's own self-description all say Adjutant AI. Nothing functional changed:
the Splunk app id, your saved searches/dashboards/models, KVStore data, and generated
artifact names are unchanged, so the upgrade is seamless.

New — run playbooks automatically, and from other Splunk apps.

  • On a schedule or on an event. A playbook can run unattended on a schedule
    (a "morning health check") or in response to a Splunk event — an alert, an ES
    correlation search, or an ITSI episode. When an event triggers it, the affected
    thing (the host, user, or entity in the alert) is handed to the playbook
    automatically, so it investigates exactly what fired. Two ready-made (disabled)
    examples are included to copy.
  • Adjutant AI as a building block for other apps. Other Splunk AI agents can now
    ask Adjutant AI to list and run your playbooks through a small, safe
    interface (an MCP server). Only playbooks you mark MCPready are exposed, every
    call must name the Org/BU it is for (which must be a business unit you have set up)
    as a safeguard, and runs go through the same governed, bounded service — never an
    open door. This interface is off by default — turn it on with one setting. When
    on, the tools can also appear inside Splunk's own MCP Server, reachable on the
    normal Splunk web address (no special port needed); you authenticate with a standard
    Splunk token. A ready-made, read-only example playbook ships enabled so there is
    always something to see the moment you switch the interface on.

New — "Report an issue" support packaging (all editions).

  • One click on any conversation (per-turn 🐞, the Ask panel, or the new Help tab)
    packages exactly what happened — versions, the resolved prompt, the tools and model used,
    the generated dashboards/searches, and every error and warning — into a single file.
  • Safe by construction: secrets are stripped before anything leaves the browser, and the
    file is encrypted to the support key, so it's safe to send over any channel.
  • It even tells you what kind of problem it looks like and matches known issues, so
    simple cases are solved without a back-and-forth.
  • Send it your way: download it and attach it to your own ticket, use the built-in
    support form, or email it. The Help tab (Report + Documentation + About) is always
    reachable — even if the app is locked by licensing.

New — ServiceNow, done properly (Professional + the servicenow feature). Read incidents,
changes, problems and the CMDB/CSDM in plain English — with bounded blast-radius / dependency
traversals ("what's the blast radius if this CI fails?"). Turn a Splunk alert, ITSI episode or ES
notable into a rich, deterministically rendered ServiceNow incident and write the number back to
the originating object (a re-fire updates, never duplicates; the closed-incident policy is
configurable). Security incidents (SIR) with MITRE ATT&CK, off until an admin enables them. Two
transports (REST or a ServiceNow MCP server), plus TISC threat-intel enrichment — all server-side
and allowlisted, so ServiceNow can never block the assistant. (Verified against the documented APIs
and unit-tested; final certification is on a live ServiceNow.)

New — run playbooks automatically, and from other apps. Playbooks can run unattended on a
schedule, or from a Splunk alert / ES correlation search / ITSI episode (the triggering entity is
handed to the run). Adjutant AI can also expose list / run over an inbound MCP server (off by
default, MCPready-only, Org/BU-scoped) — reachable inside Splunk's own MCP Server on the normal web
address, with a standard Splunk token.

New — "Report an issue" support packaging (all editions). One click packages a failing
conversation — secret-stripped and encrypted client-side — with an automatic problem
classification, plus an always-reachable Help tab even when the app is licence-locked.

New — Cribl Stream data-quality awareness (Professional+). Reads Cribl's own forwarded logs and
metrics to surface the timestamp / parse / dropped-event problems that happen inside Cribl, before
Splunk can see them — the "green in Splunk but timestamped wrong" blind spot — folded into one
readiness verdict. No Cribl Lake or Search required.

New — LLM reliability: retry, fallback & circuit breaker (Enterprise). A brief provider hiccup
(503 / 529 / rate-limit) auto-retries within a time budget; a per-config circuit breaker stops
hammering a provider that's down, then probes for recovery; and an ordered fallback transparently
switches to your next provider (and tells you which it used). Two new admin dashboards — LLM
Health and AI Activity — plus per-user / BU / org concurrency caps, all conservative and off
the critical path.

New — live model & cost catalogue (all editions). Models and prices come from a runtime catalogue
that updates without an app rebuild; automatic model discovery (Professional+) keeps it current
without ever logging your keys; an Enterprise admin screen adds price overrides and manual model
registration for private gateways.

Fixed. Generated Simple XML dashboards now share a single base search across panels (faster) and
get a top data-ingestion health panel; corrected a 3× Opus price over-charge (now server-side
authoritative, with Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 included).

1.5.0 "Data Foundation & MCP OAuth"

New: connect to OAuth 2.1‑protected MCP servers (authorization‑code + PKCE for
interactive, client‑credentials for unattended; tokens held server‑side, never in the browser
— see MCP_OAUTH.md); onboard new data sources — describe a source or attach a
sample file and get a deployment‑ready add‑on package; a "is my data parsed correctly?"
ingestion/timestamp check that reads Splunk's own internal logs; generated config validated
against your instance and given a 0–100 Data Quality Score (A–F); and attach a local
sample file in Ask (only the file name is audited, never contents).

Improved: works with the newest OpenAI "reasoning" models incl. Azure GPT‑5.4 /
GPT‑5.4‑mini (auto‑detects the request format); more reliable generated dashboards; generated
objects use the aiworkbench name tag; and Audit‑tab improvements (Business Unit
column/filter, local‑timezone timestamps, reliable token/outcome capture).

Earlier releases (1.0.0 – 1.4.3)

  • 1.4.3 — Clearer guidance and plain-language fixes when a free-tier LLM key hits its
    provider limits (e.g. Groq token-per-minute caps, Gemini zero-quota keys); the LLM config
    screen flags these up front.
  • 1.4.1 — Per-feature capability licensing with edition badges (Professional / Enterprise /
    MSP); gated features show a padlock, and nothing you created is ever deleted when a tier changes.
    Turn-level audit logging made reliable; more robust dashboard generation.
  • 1.4.0 — The assistant reads your own Splunk live (real search commands + installed
    visualizations) instead of guessing; Splunk Security Essentials detection content integrated.
  • 1.3.3 — TrackMe integration end-to-end (feed-health awareness + actions) with richer
    built-in platform knowledge.
  • 1.3.2 — First Splunkbase 1.x release: packaging and permissions hardening.
  • 1.3.1 — Fixed Org/BU edits dropping fields; safeguard to keep bundled templates correct
    after upgrades.
  • 1.3.0 — Real, per-Organisation audit logging of every AI interaction (Professional+).
  • 1.2.0 — Splunk Security Essentials content tools for templates.
  • 1.1.1 — Cisco Deep Time Series Model (CDTSM) templates: pre-trained anomaly detection and
    forecasting via the AI Toolkit, each with a proof dashboard.
  • 1.1.0 — Multi-tenancy and the Organisation / Business-Unit editor overhauled for clearer,
    safer tenant scoping.
  • 1.0.0 — The knowledge layer: ground answers in your organisation's own conventions.

(Releases before 1.0 are early pre-release history and are omitted here.)

Known issues

  • Open the assistant from inside another app. Adjutant AI is a "host shell":
    reach it from a navigation-menu entry inside Search, Enterprise Security, ITSI,
    or your own apps — not by clicking the app tile directly. Everything it creates
    lands in the namespace of the app you opened it from.
  • Some Data Foundation features need self-hosted Splunk. The
    configuration-reference grounding and config-package generation (1.5.0) read
    files on the Splunk server, so they are unavailable on Splunk Cloud; the
    assistant says so and continues with what it can.

When a published fix resolves a tracked GitHub issue, it is summarised here with
its issue number — for example: "Fixed: a dashboard panel could display raw HTML
markup as text instead of formatting it (#123)."


Short Description:
A workbench for Splunk, not just a chatbot. Analyse, correlate and build across SPL, dashboards, alerts, AI Toolkit / MLTK, ES, ITSI and TrackMe through tools that understand each one — plus any MCP server you add. Pick your LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Groq, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenRouter. Multi-tenant, multi-tier (Free, Pro, Enterprise, MSP).


Description:
Adjutant AI (formerly AI Workbench) is a generative workspace for Splunk — not a chatbot bolted onto search, but a real workbench where you investigate, analyse and build with tools that understand Splunk. It is a host shell: it has no use-cases of its own, deriving everything from the Splunk app a user opens it from and their roles. Install once on the Search Head, then embed it in the apps your users already live in — Search, ITSI, Enterprise Security, your SOC and MSP customer apps. The same engine renders a different experience per app and writes outputs into that app's namespace. Users never leave the app they came from. Ask in plain English. Get back validated SPL searches, Simple XML and Dashboard Studio dashboards, alerts, lookups, reports and Splunk AI Toolkit (MLTK) machine-learning pipelines — grounded in your running Splunk (your knowledge objects, live command syntax, CIM models), run for real before they are saved, as normal Splunk knowledge objects owned by the calling user. The depth is the difference. Where a generic MCP-only assistant talks to Splunk through one broad door, Adjutant AI ships fine-grained, Splunk-aware tools across Core, Enterprise Security, ITSI, TrackMe, ServiceNow and the AI Toolkit, each scoped to one job and run under your existing Splunk ACLs. Extend it with HTTP tools or any MCP server. New in 1.8.0 — your SOC can watch the agent. Adjutant AI emits its own activity — LLM calls, tool/MCP/ServiceNow calls, config changes, unattended run verdicts and policy refusals (the proof the controls fire) — as open-standard OCSF events to a Splunk index Enterprise Security already watches, mapped to CIM via the OCSF-CIM Add-On. On-prem, no cloud egress, off by default, resolved per Org/BU, with a shipped Behaviour dashboard. Control is the product; now it is observable. Also included: a first-class ServiceNow integration (read incidents, changes, problems and the CMDB/CSDM; turn a Splunk alert, ITSI episode or ES notable into a rich ServiceNow or SIR security incident with the number written back), governed unattended playbooks, and a Data Foundation add-on package builder. Bring your own LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Ollama (local, fully offline) or OpenRouter — server-side so API keys never leave the search head. Connecting Azure OpenAI with an API key works on every tier (Free is single-user); keyless Microsoft Entra ID / managed-identity auth for Azure OpenAI — no static secret, governed by your Entra tenant — is an Enterprise capability (new in 1.8.2). Multi-tenant by design: Organisations and Business Units resolve automatically from the calling app and roles. Free, Professional, Enterprise and MSP tiers, self-serve and air-gap-friendly.

item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

# Release Notes - v4.2.1: "The Honey Keeper" 🍯

## Summary

Version 4.2.1 is a **hotfix release** addressing a data-loss regression

introduced in v4.1.0: the `thehive_datatypes.csv` lookup could be periodically

**overwritten with default values**, wiping out user-defined custom field

mappings and causing observables to go missing from TheHive alerts and cases.

No new feature is introduced and no configuration change is required — this is

a safe, drop-in update from v4.2.0.

## Improvements & Bug Fixes

### 🗂️ Alert Actions: custom datatype mappings are no longer lost

- **Root cause**: since v4.1.0, alert actions refresh the

`thehive_datatypes.csv` lookup from the TheHive API whenever the file is

older than 24 hours. The refresh rebuilt the file **from scratch** with only

the native observable types returned by TheHive, silently destroying every

custom row (e.g. `src_ip → ip`, `dest_domain → domain`) that detections rely

on to map Splunk fields to observables. In practice the lookup was reset

every 24-72 hours, depending on when the next alert action fired.

- **Fix — non-destructive merge**: the periodic refresh is kept (it still

picks up new observable types created in TheHive), but it now **preserves

every existing row** of the lookup, custom mappings included. Only datatypes

not already listed are appended. A full regeneration never happens once the

file exists.

- **Atomic writes**: the lookup is now written to a uniquely-named temporary

file and moved into place atomically, so a crash or two concurrent alert

actions can no longer leave a truncated or half-written lookup behind.

- **Safety guard**: if the existing lookup cannot be read (locked, malformed

encoding, permissions), the refresh is **aborted** instead of overwriting

content that could not be preserved (logged as `THC-4`).

### 🧹 Minor

- Fixed a file-handle leak in the datatype lookup reader (the file was opened

on every alert action run but never closed).

## Deployment Notes

- **Prerequisite**: Python 3.9 (matches Splunk's bundled interpreter).

- **After upgrading**: if your custom `thehive_datatypes.csv` was recently

reset, restore it once from your backup — it will no longer be overwritten.

- **Migration Path**:

- **From v4.2.0 / v4.1.0 / v4.0.0**: non-breaking update. Existing

configuration, accounts, instances and certificates are preserved.

- **From v3.9.0 (Direct Upgrade)**: you can upgrade directly to v4.2.1.

- **⚠️ CRITICAL**: if upgrading from v3.x, the

**[v4.0.0 migration instructions](./v4.0.0.md) are mandatory** and remain

valid for this version (UCC architecture migration, breaking configuration

changes, and new credential storage). Please read them carefully before

proceeding.

- **Upgrade tip (Windows / on-prem)**: never delete the app's `local/` folder.

Stop Splunk, back up `local/`, deploy the new build, restore `local/`, then

start Splunk.


Description:
This TA allows to add interaction features between TheHive or Cortex (https://www.strangebee.com/) and Splunk. It allows to retrieve all kind of information from TheHive/Cortex and to perform actions on these instances using Splunk, from a search or from a predefined dashboard. This TA is supporting only TheHive 5. For having an app supporting TheHive 3 or 4, please check the oldest releases. It's also supporting the Cortex 3 version. More information here: https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex

Release Notes:

  • Added configurable bulletin messages for MMDB download outcomes
  • Added a setup selector to choose the message severity level


Short Description:
Enrich Splunk events with IPinfo's IP geolocation, ASN, privacy, residential proxy, and threat intelligence data via REST API or local MMDB lookups.


Description:
The IPinfo Splunk app brings IPinfo's API and IP database (MMDB) products into Splunk. It adds the ipinfo command, which looks up IP information for any IP address in your data. The app enriches Splunk events with geolocation, ASN, privacy, company, abuse, domains, carrier, and residential proxy data. ## Overview

Version 2.8.3 is a minor feature and security hardening release introducing native edge bundling/weighting for high-volume network environments, user-defined custom status color palettes via the Splunk Format panel UI, and strict CWE-79 input sanitization controls for Visualizer options.

## ⚡ Feature: Native Edge Bundling & Logarithmic Weight Scaling (Req-1)

AWS-DFD-Visualizer now automatically bundles overlapping connections to improve render performance and layout legibility.

- **Deduplication & Counter**: The data aggregation pipeline clusters parallel records sharing identical source and target endpoints into a single edge containing a `count` attribute.

- **Logarithmic Stroke Weight**: Links scale their rendered path thickness logarithmically based on the row count:

```javascript

strokeWidth \= Math.min(10, 2 + Math.log2(count + 1))

```

Single rows draw at a baseline 2.5px width, while high-volume traffic (50+ rows) scales up to 10px to visually signify volume. React owns this visual SVG attribute directly (React-D3 SoC rule preserved).

- **Hover Count Badge**: Hovering on a weighted edge displays a blue tooltip/badge containing the aggregated row counts (e.g. `×42 rows`) under the connection label.

Enables dynamic, UI-driven color overrides for custom telemetry status codes.
